narrative.summary: India has no AI-specific statute; its binding AI rules sit in the Information Technology Rules and sector regulation. Since 20 February 2026 the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules require platforms to label synthetically generated content and carry provenance markers, with a further amendment still in draft, and MeitY advisories of March 2024 and March 2026 add expectations on AI models and deepfakes. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 and its 2025 Rules apply in phases from November 2025, with most duties from May 2027. Policy is set by the India AI Governance Guidelines (November 2025), the IndiaAI Mission and its Safety Institute, MeitY's AI Governance and Economic Group (2026), NITI Aayog's 2018 national strategy and Responsible AI papers, and white papers of the Principal Scientific Adviser on a techno-legal approach to AI governance. Sector regulators add rules and guidance: SEBI regulations making intermediaries responsible for the AI tools they use, the Reserve Bank's FREE-AI framework and draft model-risk guidance, CDSCO's medical device software guidance, ICMR's ethics guidelines for AI in health, TRAI recommendations, CERT-In AI security guidance and a Competition Commission market study. States including Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Kerala and Haryana have their own AI policies, missions and government orders.

Searches were made in English and Hindi. Several official websites could not be read automatically, including most state government portals, the IndiaAI document store, the Election Commission and the insurance regulator. Records from those sources are marked as located but not fully read, or held as pending. instruments.official_title: India AI Governance Guidelines: Enabling Safe and Trusted AI Innovation
instruments.english_title: India AI Governance Guidelines: Enabling Safe and Trusted AI Innovation
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (IndiaAI Mission); prepared by the drafting committee constituted by MeitY in July 2025 (chair: Prof. Balaraman Ravindran), unveiled with the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser
instruments.publisher_name: IndiaAI (Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology)
instruments.current_status: Unveiled by MeitY under the IndiaAI Mission on 5 November 2025 (PIB release of that date, which links the PIB-hosted copy). The 68-page text was read from the copy published by the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser (byte-identical to the PIB-hosted copy at https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/nov/doc2025115685601.pdf). The IndiaAI article page links IndiaAI's own copy (https://indiaai.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/docs/guidelines-governance.pdf), which refused access (HTTP 403) on 10 October 2026. The guidelines are not a statute or rule: they state that a separate AI law is not needed at this stage and rely on existing laws, voluntary measures and techno-legal tools. Its recommended AI Governance Group was constituted as the AI Governance and Economic Group by MeitY Office Memorandum of 13 April 2026. Supersedes the January 2025 sub-committee draft report.
instruments.summary: MeitY's framework for AI governance in India, in four parts: seven 'sutras' adapted from the RBI FREE-AI report (trust, people first, innovation over restraint, fairness and equity, accountability, understandable by design, safety/resilience/sustainability); recommendations across six pillars (infrastructure, capacity building, policy and regulation, risk mitigation, accountability, institutions); a short-, medium- and long-term action plan; and practical guidelines for industry and regulators. It concludes that a separate AI law is not needed at this stage, recommends targeted amendments (e.g. IT Act classification of AI actors, copyright for training), an India-specific risk framework, an AI incidents database, a graded liability system and voluntary commitments backed by techno-legal measures. It proposes an inter-ministerial AI Governance Group supported by a Technology & Policy Expert Committee, with the AI Safety Institute providing technical expertise and sector regulators keeping enforcement powers.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Indian national instrument shaping AI governance (government-governance, ethics, risk-assurance, generative-ai).

instruments.official_title: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
instruments.english_title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament of India
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Law and Justice (Legislative Department), Gazette of India
instruments.current_status: Act No. 22 of 2023, assented to and published in the Gazette of India (Extraordinary, Part II, Section 1, No. 25) on 11 August 2023. Commenced in phases by G.S.R. 843(E) of 13 November 2025: s.1(2), s.2, ss.18-26 (Data Protection Board), ss.35, 38-43 and s.44(1) and (3) in force from 13 November 2025; s.6(9) (consent managers) and s.27(1)(d) one year after publication (13 November 2026); the main obligations of Data Fiduciaries and rights of Data Principals (ss.3-5, 6(1)-(8) and (10), 7-17, 27 except (1)(d), 28-34, 36, 37, 44(2)) eighteen months after publication (13 May 2027). The Digital Personal Data Protection (Removal of Difficulties) Order, 2026 (S.O. 5458(E), dated 5 October 2026, Gazette of 6 October 2026, in force on publication) made two textual corrections: s.9(1) now reads 'child or of a person with disability' and s.10(2)(c)(ii) 'data audit'. Neither the Act nor its amendments mention artificial intelligence; it is recorded as the general data protection law governing AI training and use on personal data. MeitY copy: https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2024/06/2bf1f0e9f04e6fb4f8fef35e82c42aa5.pdf
instruments.summary: India's first general data protection statute: it governs processing of digital personal data in India and of data processed abroad in connection with offering goods or services in India, on the basis of consent or listed legitimate uses, and excludes personal data the data principal has made publicly available (s.3(c)(ii)). Data Fiduciaries must give notice, secure data, report breaches, erase data when the purpose ends and obtain verifiable parental consent for children's data; Significant Data Fiduciaries must appoint a Data Protection Officer, an independent data auditor and carry out periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments. It creates the Data Protection Board of India to inquire into breaches and impose penalties of up to INR 250 crore per contravention (Schedule).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law; governs the use of personal data for AI training and deployment, including the public-data exclusion and the Significant Data Fiduciary regime.

instruments.english_title: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E))
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
instruments.current_status: Notified by G.S.R. 846(E) of 13 November 2025 (Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3(i), No. 760) under s.40 of the DPDP Act, after the draft of 3 January 2025. Rules 1, 2 and 17-21 (Board and its procedure) in force on publication; rule 4 (consent managers) one year after publication (13 November 2026); rules 3, 5-16, 22 and 23 eighteen months after publication (13 May 2027). Corrected by corrigenda G.S.R. 892(E) dated 10 December 2025 (Gazette No. 806 of 11 December 2025; MeitY lists it as 16 December 2025). MeitY copy: https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/11/53450e6e5dc0bfa85ebd78686cadad39.pdf
instruments.summary: Implementing rules for the DPDP Act covering privacy notices, registration and duties of consent managers, verifiable parental consent for children's data, reasonable security safeguards, 72-hour breach reporting to the Board, data retention and erasure, and the functioning of the Data Protection Board as a digital office. Rule 13 requires Significant Data Fiduciaries to carry out an annual Data Protection Impact Assessment and audit, to exercise due diligence that technical measures 'including algorithmic software' used to process personal data do not pose a risk to data principals' rights, and to localise personal data specified by the Government. Rule 16 and the Second Schedule exempt processing for research, archiving or statistical purposes carried on to the specified standards.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Contains an explicit algorithmic-software due-diligence duty and DPIA/audit duties for Significant Data Fiduciaries; research exemption relevant to AI training.

instruments.official_title: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021
instruments.english_title: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 (G.S.R. 139(E))
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
instruments.current_status: Notified by G.S.R. 139(E) of 25 February 2021 under s.87 of the IT Act, 2000, superseding the Intermediaries Guidelines Rules, 2011; in force on publication. Amended by G.S.R. 794(E) (28 October 2022), G.S.R. 275(E) (6 April 2023), G.S.R. 775(E) (22 October 2025, authorised officers for rule 3(1)(d)) and G.S.R. 120(E) (10 February 2026, synthetically generated information; in force 20 February 2026), corrected by G.S.R. 148(E) of 26 February 2026. MeitY consolidated text 'updated 10.02.2026, Corrigenda 26.02.2026': https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/03/0b576f2071694b52e4cd6bb1b6dfab1e.pdf. A further draft amendment (Second Amendment Rules, 2026) was under consultation in March-May 2026; no final notification found as of 10 October 2026.
instruments.summary: Sets the due-diligence conditions intermediaries must meet to keep safe-harbour protection under s.79 of the IT Act, including user notice of prohibited content, takedown on court orders or government intimation, grievance redressal and Grievance Appellate Committees, plus extra duties for significant social media intermediaries; Part III sets a Code of Ethics for digital news and online curated content publishers. As amended in 2026, the Rules define 'synthetically generated information' and require intermediaries offering AI generation tools to block unlawful synthetic content and to label and embed provenance metadata in other synthetic content (rule 3(3)), and require significant social media intermediaries to obtain and verify user declarations of synthetic content (rule 4(1A)); takedown on actual knowledge is cut to three hours.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: India's main binding rules on AI-generated content (deepfakes) on online platforms, via intermediary due-diligence obligations.

instruments.official_title: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2026
instruments.english_title: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2026 (G.S.R. 120(E)) - synthetically generated information
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
instruments.current_status: Notified by G.S.R. 120(E) of 10 February 2026 (Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3(i), No. 114; F. No. 2(5)/2025-CyberLaws); in force 20 February 2026. Corrected by corrigenda G.S.R. 148(E) of 26 February 2026 (eGazette 2026/270525: references to the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita read as the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita read with the BNSS). Finalises the draft of 22 October 2025. MeitY published FAQs on 10 February 2026. MeitY copy: https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/02/f55fe52418b03f58b0669f6a8bc03b6d.pdf
instruments.summary: Amends the IT Rules, 2021 to define 'synthetically generated information' (audio, visual or audio-visual content artificially or algorithmically created or altered so that it appears real), with carve-outs for routine editing, accessibility and good-faith document preparation, and confirms that removing such content with automated tools does not forfeit safe harbour. Intermediaries whose resources enable creating synthetic content must deploy technical measures to prevent unlawful synthetic content (child sexual abuse material, non-consensual intimate imagery, false documents, explosives, deceptive impersonation) and must prominently label all other synthetic content and embed permanent metadata or provenance identifiers that users cannot remove; significant social media intermediaries must require user declarations, verify them technically and label synthetic content before publication. It also shortens takedown on court orders or government intimation from 36 to three hours, grievance disposal from 15 to seven days, and removal of non-consensual intimate content from 24 to two hours.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding labelling, provenance and prevention duties for AI-generated content on Indian platforms.

instruments.official_title: Draft amendments to IT Rules, 2021 relating to Synthetically generated information
instruments.english_title: Draft amendments to the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 relating to synthetically generated information (October 2025)

Superseded by the final Amendment Rules, 2026 (G.S.R. 120(E), 10 February 2026), which dropped the fixed 10% label-size requirement and added prevention duties for unlawful synthetic content. Notice: https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/10/38be31bac9d39bbe22f24fc42442d5d1.pdf; explanatory note: https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/10/8e40cdd134cd92dd783a37556428c370.pdf Publication date source (date audit 2026-10-13): MeitY consultation notice (companion PDF to the draft): 'Dated: 22nd October, 2025' (draft rules themselves say 'New Delhi, the ___th October, 2025').
instruments.summary: MeitY draft amending the IT Rules, 2021 to define 'synthetically generated information' and require intermediaries that offer tools to create or modify it to label such content and embed a permanent unique metadata identifier, with the label covering at least 10% of the visual display or the first 10% of an audio clip. Significant social media intermediaries would have had to obtain user declarations on whether uploads are synthetic, verify them with technical measures and label confirmed synthetic content.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Consultation draft of India's deepfake labelling rules.

instruments.official_title: Draft amendments to the IT Rules, 2021 in relation to strengthening intermediary compliance with clarifications, advisories and directions issued by the Ministry and digital media oversight
instruments.english_title: Draft IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Second Amendment Rules, 2026 (intermediary compliance with Ministry advisories, SGI label display and digital media oversight)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
instruments.current_status: First draft published 30 March 2026 (https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/03/30591fc6e322dcbcc9dae84a0f02e9e7.pdf) with comments due 14 April 2026, extended on 10 April 2026 to 29 April 2026. instruments.summary: Proposed 'Second Amendment Rules, 2026' to the IT Rules, 2021: a new rule 3(4) would make compliance with written MeitY clarifications, advisories, directions, SOPs, codes of practice and guidelines part of intermediaries' safe-harbour due diligence, and retention duties in rule 3(1)(g)-(h) would apply without prejudice to other laws. The 21 April 2026 revision would require labels on synthetically generated visual content to be continuously and clearly displayed throughout the content, and Part III changes would extend digital-media oversight to news and current-affairs content posted by non-publisher users and widen the Inter-Departmental Committee's remit.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Would tighten deepfake label display and give MeitY advisories (including AI advisories) binding due-diligence force.

instruments.official_title: Due diligence by Intermediaries / Platforms under the Information Technology Act, 2000 and Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 (Advisory eNo.2(4)/2023-CyberLaws-3, 15 March 2024)
instruments.english_title: MeitY advisory on due diligence by intermediaries and platforms on AI models, LLMs and generative AI (eNo.2(4)/2023-CyberLaws-3, 15 March 2024)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (Cyber Law and Data Governance Group)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
instruments.current_status: Advisory dated 15 March 2024 issued 'in supersession of' advisory eNo.2(4)/2023-CyberLaws-3 dated 1 March 2024, and in addition to advisory No. 2(4)/2023-CyberLaws-2 of 26 December 2023 (cited as Annexure A but not included in this 2-page file). Addressed to intermediaries and platforms; paragraph 5 states they 'are hereby required to ensure compliance with the above with immediate effect', while the specific measures are worded as 'advised'/'should'. It has no stated statutory force beyond the IT Act and IT Rules it refers to. Scanned file hosted on meity.gov.in (static/uploads/2024/02); no MeitY listing page for it was found via the site search.
instruments.summary: Advises every intermediary and platform to ensure that AI models, LLMs, generative AI, software or algorithms on their resources do not let users share unlawful content under rule 3(1)(b) of the IT Rules, do not permit bias or discrimination or threaten the integrity of the electoral process, and that under-tested or unreliable AI models are made available in India only with labels (and optionally consent pop-ups) about the possible fallibility of their output. Intermediaries enabling synthetic text, audio, visual or audio-visual content that could be used as misinformation or deepfakes are advised to label it or embed permanent unique metadata identifying the intermediary's resource and, where users modify it, the user.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: MeitY's principal advisory on AI model deployment and deepfake labelling before the 2026 rules.

instruments.official_title: Frequently Asked Questions on the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2026
instruments.english_title: FAQs on the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2026 (synthetically generated information), 10 February 2026
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

instruments.summary: Thirty questions and answers explaining the 2026 amendments: the definition of synthetically generated information and its exclusions, which intermediaries are covered by the new rule 3(3), the categories of unlawful synthetic content to be prevented, labelling and metadata requirements, the new rule 4(1A) declaration and verification duties for significant social media intermediaries, and the shortened takedown and grievance timelines. It gives worked examples of content that does and does not count as synthetic, such as face-swapped videos versus routine edits, translation or accessibility features.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Official interpretive guidance on India's deepfake labelling rules.

instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (Cyber Laws Division)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
instruments.current_status: Advisory dated 16 March 2026 addressed to all intermediaries, issued 'with the approval of the Competent Authority'. instruments.summary: Warns all intermediaries that computer resources under their control have been used to generate and spread abusive, defamatory, objectionable, derogatory and misleading synthetically generated information, and lists the rules engaged: user notice duties (rules 3(1)(c)-(cb)), three-hour takedown (3(1)(d)), prevention and labelling of synthetic content (3(3)) and declaration and verification by significant social media intermediaries (4(1A)). It advises intermediaries to stop hosting the flagged content, set up enhanced monitoring, enforce terms of service and AI usage restrictions (including suspension or termination of violating accounts) and remove unlawful AI-generated content without destroying evidence, reminding them that non-compliance removes s.79 safe harbour under rule 7.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Enforcement-oriented advisory applying the 2026 synthetic-content rules to AI generation services.

It is chaired by the Minister of Electronics & IT, with the MoS as vice-chair and the Principal Scientific Adviser, Chief Economic Adviser, CEO NITI Aayog, the Secretaries of Telecommunications, Economic Affairs and Science & Technology, an NSCS representative and the MeitY Secretary (member convener) as members. Its terms of reference include coordinating AI policy across ministries and sectoral regulators, issuing guidelines on firms' accountability for compliance with local laws, studying emerging risks, regulatory gaps and needed legal amendments, developing India's AI governance position, a ten-year AI deployment roadmap, classifying AI use cases as 'deploy', 'pilot' or 'defer', and assessing labour-market impacts.

instruments.official_title: Strengthening AI Governance through Techno-Legal Framework

instruments.summary: Proposes a 'techno-legal' approach to AI governance for India, in which legal and policy requirements are embedded in technical design and tooling across the AI lifecycle rather than relying only on command-and-control regulation. It maps existing baseline laws (IT Act 2000, BNS 2023, DPDP Act 2023), sectoral guidance and the India AI Governance Guidelines 2025, sets out technological pathways for safe and trusted AI, and describes how the proposed institutions - AI Governance Group, Technology and Policy Expert Committee, AI Safety Institute, a national AI incidents database and voluntary commitments - would operationalise it.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Indian national instrument shaping AI governance (government-governance, risk-assurance, transparency).

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Technical review notes: Backfill run in five parts (N1 laws and rules; N2 MeitY and IndiaAI; N3 NITI Aayog, PSA, TEC and other national papers; N4 sector regulators; N5 states). The first attempt on 2026-10-08 was stopped by a usage limit before any fragment was written; on 2026-10-10 all five parts were rebuilt from freshly read official texts, reusing earlier downloads only after re-fetching or re-reading them, so no record written before the restart remained unchecked. index-readiness: no government-published AI readiness index or maturity assessment was found (NITI and MeitY listings searched). Access problems: meity.gov.in renders client-side and returns 200 for any path, so documents were located through the site's own document API and read from www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads; IndiaAI's S3 document store (indiaai.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com) returned 403, so the January 2025 sub-committee report and the public-sector AI competency framework are primary_source_located; TEC releases the final TEC 57090:2025 text only after a registration form, so that record is built from TEC's standards listing and the consultation draft; RBI PDFs sit behind a bot challenge, so RBI records cite the RBI HTML pages carrying the full text; eci.gov.in returned 406 and irdai.gov.in 504, so ECI deepfake advisories and IRDAI AI items are leads; egazette.gov.in needs an extra CA bundle. States: most state portals refused connections from this environment. All tn.gov.in hosts were unreachable, so the two Tamil Nadu records (2020 Safe and Ethical AI Policy, G.O. 25/2024 TN AI Mission) were located through indexed copies of the official files and are primary_source_located with link_status inaccessible. Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Telangana (beyond the 2020 framework), Odisha, Rajasthan and Assam portals could not be read; their AI instruments are leads. Punjab, Delhi, West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh were searched by web search only. The OPSA white papers were found by two parts and deduplicated; the AI Impact Summit Declaration (19 Feb 2026) is recorded under IND international as a summit outcome hosted by India. BIS adoptions of ISO/IEC 42001, 23894 and 22989 appear in BIS listings without dates, so they are leads. The IT Act 2000 has no explicit AI provisions and is recorded only as the parent Act of the IT Rules; the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam and Telecommunications Act 2023 were not checked for AI wording. Two MeitY advisories (26 Dec 2023, 1 Mar 2024) have no official copy online and are leads; the 15 Mar 2024 advisory that replaced them is recorded.
